page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the weak category (bottom 25%). Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression is poor (bottom 10%). However, the instance demonstrates average performance (middle 50%) in multi-core workloads, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the average tier, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 984.37 GB/sec.

The hardware profile and benchmark data suggest that the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that can leverage parallel processing rather than high single-thread performance. Favorable multi-core and memory bandwidth results support database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving, all of which scored in the average tier. Conversely, tasks requiring rapid single-threaded execution or local storage are less optimal due to the weak single-core performance and lack of bundled local disks.
